hook.text: In 2006, a spinach E. coli outbreak took 2 weeks to trace to one farm. Today, blockchain could do it in 2 seconds.

buildup.text: Traceability means tracking food one step forward and one step back through the supply chain—from ingredient source to customer.

discovery.text: Lot codes and batch numbers link finished products to specific ingredients, production dates, and supplier deliveries.

twist.text: The EU requires full traceability. The US only requires 'one-up, one-back'—your supplier and customer, not the full chain.

climax.text: Walmart now requires leafy green suppliers to use blockchain traceability. Trace time dropped from 7 days to 2.2 seconds.

punchline.text: When outbreaks hit, traceability means seconds of response, not days.

quiz.question: How did blockchain change Walmart's food traceability?
options: Trace time dropped from 7 days to 2.2 seconds for leafy greens
